claims.claim: Homeowners can sign a mortgage deed electronically.
claims.quote: It’s all done on your computer or mobile phone.
claims.note: The homeowner guide says the signing process is on a computer or mobile phone.

claims.claim: HM Land Registry provides the digital mortgage service.
claims.quote: Sign your mortgage deed is HM Land Registry’s digital mortgage service.
claims.note: The publication explicitly identifies the service as HM Land Registry’s.

claims.claim: Digital signing removes the need for a wet signature on a paper deed.
claims.quote: You do not have to wait for the paperwork to arrive in the post, sign it in front of a witness and send it back to your conveyancer or lender.
claims.note: The guide explicitly removes the paper signing and return steps.

claims.claim: The service is available to homeowners remortgaging.
claims.quote: You can use the service to remortgage your property.
claims.note: The guide explicitly states remortgaging use.

claims.claim: The service is available to borrowers purchasing a property.
claims.note: The supplied text mentions remortgaging but does not establish use for a property purchase.

claims.claim: The borrower’s lender must use the HM Land Registry digital mortgage service.
claims.quote: Your bank or building society and conveyancer must use the Sign your mortgage deed service.
claims.note: The guide requires the lender to use the service, alongside the conveyancer.

claims.claim: A GOV.UK One Login account is required to verify identity before signing.
claims.quote: You will need to prove your identity using GOV.UK One Login . Using GOV.UK One Login is safe. Request a code You will be logged into the HM Land Registry service when you’ve verified your identity.
claims.note: The guide names GOV.UK One Login for identity verification before deed signing.
